item.title: Marin County Arts & Crafts Fair — Thu Nov 19, 11:00 AM — Marin County Employee Arts & Crafts Fair
item.description:
Have fun, enjoy music, and discover handmade treasures! The Marin County Employee Arts & Crafts Fair returns November 18–19, from 11 a.m.–4 p.m., at the Marin Civic Center cafeteria, Room 237, in San Rafael.
Shop handcrafts and original art while listening to the County Crows employee band. Different vendors and music each day--visit twice!
Craving something sweet? The HR & Friends Bake charity sale and individual bakers sell treats on Wednesday only.
Celebrating its 26th anniversary, this staff-founded tradition is open to the public. Employees participate on their own time, and volunteers in the county's MarinShares program provide support.
Browse original paintings, drawings, woodcuts, and photographs. Crafts include ceramics, jewelry, paper art, potted plants, crocheted dolls, notecards, candles, knitted and crocheted wearables, and lots more.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Dying to Talk About It Community Conversation — Thu Nov 19, 2:30 PM — Healdsburg Senior Center
item.description:
You already know everything you need to walk in the door.
No preparation. No expertise. No right answers.
Dying to Talk About It is a facilitated conversation where neighbors come together to speak honestly about death and dying – what we fear, what we hope for, what we’ve witnessed, and what we carry.
What you bring to this room matters. Your stories, your questions, your silence — all of it has a place here. A trained facilitator holds the space so the conversation can go somewhere real.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Turkey 101 with Chef Charlie Palmer at Appellation — Thu Nov 19, 4:00 PM — 101 Dovetail Lane
item.description:
Turkey 101 with Chef Charlie Palmer at Appellation Healdsburg offers a hands-on Thanksgiving cooking master class led by acclaimed Chef Charlie Palmer. Limited to just ten guests, the experience covers essential turkey preparation techniques, including brining, breaking down a whole bird, trussing, and roasting it to a beautifully caramelized finish. Winemaker Tom Rochioli will pour wines paired with the turkey, featuring the same wine he serves at his own Thanksgiving table. Guests will gain practical culinary skills and confidence to prepare a memorable holiday feast at home.
Source: Sonoma.com, North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Singles Bingo + Switch — Bingo with a Touch of Speed Dating ages 30-49 — Thu Nov 19, 6:45 PM — Trailhouse
item.description:
**Singles Bingo + Switch | Bingo with a Touch of Speed Dating**
Sick of Dating Apps?
Join Catch Singles and North Bay Bingo for a fun, interactive evening at Trailhouse Café in Santa Rosa. We’re putting a fresh spin on traditional speed dating by combining bingo, rotating seats, and plenty of opportunities to connect.
As bingo rounds end, participants switch seats, giving everyone a chance to meet new people naturally. No awkward interviews or forced conversations — just good company, a little friendly competition, and the possibility of meeting someone special.
After bingo, stick around for a relaxed social mixer to continue conversations and make new connections!
**Thursday, November 19 | 7:00–9:30 PM** (check in 6:45) Trailhouse Café | Santa Rosa Singles ages 30–49 $40 per person | Includes one beverage
Limited spots available. Advance registration required.
**Hosted by Catch Singles — Bringing local singles together, one event at a time.**
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press

item.title: Greg Mendez & Haley Heynderickx — Thu Nov 19, 7:00 PM — Little Saint
item.description:
Haley Heynderickx is a singer-songwriter known for her intricate fingerstyle guitar work and quietly expressive songwriting. Her music balances intimacy and subtle humor, shaped by solitude, close observation, and the gentle rhythms of everyday life. After years of extensive touring, she released her acclaimed album Seed of a Seed in 2024. In 2025, she followed it with a collaborative record alongside Max Garcia Conover, and she is currently writing and recording her third full-length album.

item.description:
The Harvest Circle: Well, Wealthy & Wise is an intimate autumn gathering in downtown Petaluma, guided by Holly Shantara. Part of The W.E.L.L. Series, the evening celebrates wisdom, energy, leadership and legacy while inviting guests to reflect on personal growth and set intentions for the future. Activities include a seasonal teaching, guided visualization, sharing circle, grounding ritual and a personal intuitive micro-reading for each guest. An optional cacao ceremony is also available. No prior experience is necessary, and guests are welcome to come as they are. Doors open at 6 p.m., with seating limited to 16 participants.

item.description:
Holiday Open House + Marketplace at Grand Cru Custom Crush offers a festive afternoon of wine tasting, holiday shopping and local food. Guests can sample wines from participating wineries, browse unique gifts from local makers and artisans, and enjoy food and charcuterie while supporting small businesses. Participating wineries include Aston Estate, Bienvenue, Boars’ View, Bruliam, Bucher, Copper Six, Fat Dragon, DuMOL, Jeff Cohn, Moret Brealynn, Parea and Stringer, with additional wineries to be announced. The holiday marketplace features local vendors offering distinctive gifts, handcrafted goods and specialty products. Tickets include admission and wine tastings from participating wineries. Food, additional wine purchases and marketplace items are available for purchase separately. The event provides an opportunity to discover local wines, find holiday gifts and celebrate the season with the community.

item.title: Booked & Bottled: Build a Blind Date at Coursey Graves — Sat Nov 21, 2:00 PM — 6860 Serenity Way
item.description:
Booked & Bottled at Coursey Graves Estate Winery pairs wine tasting with the fun of discovering a mystery book. Guests sample wines matched to literary genres, including Chardonnay with historical fiction, Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir with romantasy, Syrah with contemporary fiction, and Napa Cabernet with thrillers. After choosing a favorite pour, guests select a mystery book and personalize it with book-themed extras such as bookmarks, stickers, and tea. Each book is wrapped and includes a pairing card explaining the connection between the wine and story. The book remains a surprise until unwrapped at home. Tickets include a wine flight, a full glass of wine, food, a wrapped book with accessories, book-themed games, and access to a book swap. Additional mystery books are available for purchase. Limited to 50 tickets. Ages 21 and older.
Source: Sonoma.com

item.description:
Community members are invited to participate in Community Milling Day on October 25 or November 22 at The Olive Press. Guests can bring their own olive harvest to be milled alongside others, contributing to a shared production of fresh extra virgin olive oil.
